value_chain_position: Diversified base-metal major transitioning to a copper-weighted mix, still carrying a large zinc business.
cost_curve_verified: The screener proxy understates the cost position: it reads a trailing-twelve-month operating margin of 46.2%, while Teck's own second-quarter 2026 release (2026-07-23) reports a copper net cash unit cost of US$1.64 per pound, down from US$2.02 a year earlier, full-year 2026 guidance of US$1.85-2.20 per pound, and a 61% quarterly margin - the proxy and the company disagree, and the company figure is the better one. A second, larger disagreement: the input bundle asserts net debt of C$3.74 billion, but the company reports total debt of C$4,808 million (including C$965 million of leases) against C$6,052 million of cash for a net CASH position of C$1,244 million at 2026-06-30; the vendor balance sheet mis-maps roughly C$5 billion of non-debt liabilities into borrowings, and this note uses the company figure.
gm_trajectory: Improving on both axes, which is the healthy combination: second-quarter 2026 revenue of C$3.605 billion was up 78% on the C$2.023 billion of a year earlier, while operating margin (adjusted operating profit before depreciation, divided by revenue) widened to about 61% from about 36%; the sequence over the last four reported quarters runs roughly 50%, 53% and 61%, versus the 46.2% trailing average the proxy still carries.
bull_thesis: Teck is a genuinely repaired operating business trading at a discount to the copper majors, and it is being converted into a bigger, better-rated one at a fixed exchange ratio. Three things carry the case. First, the operations have turned. After a 2025 in which the Quebrada Blanca tailings facility repeatedly forced production cuts, Teck ran a comprehensive operational review in October 2025 and rebased its plans on, in management's words, demonstrated performance rather than design rates. Since then it has delivered three consecutive stable quarters at Quebrada Blanca (55,000, 56,000 and 55,800 tonnes of copper), reaffirmed 2026-2028 guidance in January 2026, and driven copper net cash unit costs down to US$1.64 per pound in the second quarter of 2026 from US$2.02 a year earlier. Adjusted operating profit before depreciation more than doubled to C$2.193 billion in that quarter on C$3.605 billion of revenue, and adjusted earnings of US$1.39 per share beat a US$0.77 consensus. Second, the asset base is long-lived and irreplaceable: Highland Valley extended to 2046 at an average 132,000 tonnes of copper a year, Quebrada Blanca with a tax stability agreement to 2037 and a resource management says supports multiple expansions, Red Dog still one of the world's best zinc mines, and Trail Operations restored to profit and now backed by a July 2026 agreement with the Canada Growth Fund to expand germanium, gallium and antimony output. All of this is funded from a net cash balance sheet - C$1,244 million net cash and C$10.3 billion of liquidity - while a peak construction year is under way. Third, the merger. Teck shareholders receive 1.3301 Anglo American shares for each Teck share under a court-approved plan of arrangement that both shareholder bases approved on 2025-12-09. At Anglo American's price of 3,907 pence on 2026-08-04 and a sterling rate of 1.3443, that consideration is worth about US$69.86 per Teck share against a Teck price of US$65.19 - a gap of roughly 7% that closes on the single outstanding regulatory approval, which the companies said on 2026-07-30 is expected between September 2026 and March 2027. Beyond the gap sit US$800 million a year of announced corporate synergies and a roadmap to a further US$1.4 billion a year from combining Quebrada Blanca with the neighbouring Collahuasi mine. Two free options sit on top: the QB-Collahuasi adjacency, and a legacy royalty portfolio that includes a 10% net profits interest (rising to 15% after six million ounces) over ground overlapping Barrick's Fourmile gold discovery in Nevada, which press reporting suggests could generate US$100-200 million a year at full production and which no published valuation of Teck contains. The conditions the case depends on: copper holding somewhere near current levels, the sand dam at Quebrada Blanca finishing on schedule by year-end 2026, and Chinese antitrust clearance arriving without punitive remedies.
bear_thesis: The bear case is not that Teck is a bad company. It is that you are being asked to buy a price-taker at the top of its price. Copper traded at US$6.65 a pound on 2026-08-04 - its 52-week high, 53% above the US$4.36 low - and the entire copper cohort rose 5-8% in that one session, Teck itself by 8.3%. Every flattering number in the bull case is a function of that print. Teck's own torque measure says a 10% move in the metal swings operating profit by about 14%, and that arithmetic runs in both directions. Price the downside properly. Take copper back to US$4.50 a pound, roughly where it traded twelve months ago, and hold unit costs at US$2.10 (costs are sticky on the way down; diesel is already flagged as a 2026 headwind). Copper margin falls to US$2.40 a pound; on roughly 1,050 million pounds of consolidated production that is US$2.52 billion, or C$3.55 billion, against C$5.70 billion in the base case. Deduct the 40% of Quebrada Blanca that belongs to Sumitomo and Codelco - about C$0.85 billion at that copper price - and copper contributes C$2.70 billion. Zinc at US$1.10 a pound with Trail marginal contributes about C$0.80 billion, and corporate costs take C$0.40 billion, leaving attributable operating profit of roughly C$3.10 billion against a C$5.28 billion base case and a C$8.6 billion annualised first-half 2026 run rate. That is a 45-50% collapse, which is exactly what a torque of 1.4 times a 32% metal decline produces. At 6.5 times - a fair trough multiple - that is C$20.2 billion of enterprise value, or about US$29.70 a share, and the net cash cushion largely disappears because Highland Valley is consuming C$900 million to C$1.2 billion of capital in 2026 alone plus C$450-500 million of capitalised stripping. Add back a discounted royalty book and the shares are worth roughly US$32 - a 51% fall from here, and almost precisely Teck's own 52-week low of US$30.98. Nothing in the merger prevents this: the consideration is 1.3301 Anglo American shares, not a fixed sum of money, and Anglo American falls in the same tape. There are company-specific risks layered on top. The Quebrada Blanca tailings facility has slipped repeatedly since the first quarter of 2025 and the sand dam still has to be finished by year-end 2026 - Deutsche Bank's Liam Fitzpatrick was still asking in February 2026 whether extra rock benches would be needed. Highland Valley's sanctioned capital already came in 15-20% above the strategy-day estimate, in a sector where that pattern rarely stops at one revision. The advertised US$1.4 billion a year from combining Quebrada Blanca with Collahuasi rests on a commercial agreement that does not exist and whose economic split with Glencore, Anglo and Mitsui is unnegotiated - Jefferies pressed on this in October 2025 and management conceded it was still to be worked out; it was still unresolved in April 2026. Chinese antitrust clearance is the last approval standing and China is the largest buyer of the concentrate this combination will control; conditional approvals with divestment or behavioural remedies are a live possibility. And free cash flow conversion is already poor at 24% of operating profit. Confirmation of the bear case would be copper losing US$5.50 a pound, a further tailings deadline slipping past 2026, or remedies attached to the Chinese decision.
sop_bull: About US$81 a share (C$114 a share), assuming copper sustains US$6.25 a pound and zinc US$1.55, with the combined company re-rating toward a copper-major multiple. Parts, in Canadian dollars: copper operations contribute roughly C$6.46 billion of operating profit before depreciation on about 1,080 million pounds at a US$4.25 per pound margin, less C$1.44 billion for the 40% of Quebrada Blanca owned by Sumitomo and Codelco, leaving C$5.02 billion; zinc (Red Dog plus Trail plus silver, germanium and indium by-products) contributes C$1.53 billion; corporate costs take C$0.40 billion; attributable operating profit of C$6.15 billion at 8.0 times is C$49.2 billion of enterprise value, or about US$72.40 a share on 483 million shares. Add net cash of C$1.24 billion (US$1.83 a share), the royalty portfolio including the Fourmile net profits interest at C$1.75 billion (US$2.57 a share), and C$3.0 billion (US$4.41 a share) for Teck's 37.6% share of the US$800 million of announced annual synergies plus a partial credit for the Quebrada Blanca-Collahuasi adjacency. Total about US$81.
sop_bear: About US$32 a share (C$44 a share), assuming the copper cycle turns against it - copper back to US$4.50 a pound and zinc to US$1.10, with unit costs sticky at US$2.10. Parts, in Canadian dollars: copper contributes C$3.55 billion of operating profit before depreciation (about 1,050 million pounds at a US$2.40 per pound margin), less C$0.85 billion for the 40% Quebrada Blanca minority, leaving C$2.70 billion; zinc contributes C$0.80 billion with Trail near break-even; corporate costs take C$0.40 billion; attributable operating profit of C$3.10 billion at 6.5 times is C$20.2 billion of enterprise value, about US$29.70 a share. The net cash position is largely consumed by the Highland Valley programme (C$900 million to C$1.2 billion in 2026 plus C$450-500 million of capitalised stripping), so credit only C$0.5 billion (US$0.74 a share); the royalty book is discounted to C$0.75 billion (US$1.10 a share) because a lower gold and metals tape pushes Fourmile further out. Total about US$32 - which is a 51% fall from US$65.19 and sits at Teck's own 52-week low of US$30.98.
sop_fair_value: US$70 a share (roughly C$98), reached independently by two routes that converge.
sop_breakdown: Route one, the operating sum-of-the-parts at a mid-cycle copper price of US$5.75 a pound and zinc of US$1.35 (both below the US$6.65 and current spot but above the multi-year average): copper operations produce about C$5.70 billion of operating profit before depreciation on roughly 1,080 million pounds at a US$3.75 per pound margin; deduct C$1.27 billion for the 40% of Quebrada Blanca owned by Sumitomo and Codelco, leaving C$4.43 billion. Zinc - Red Dog, Trail and the silver, germanium and indium by-product stream - adds C$1.25 billion. Corporate costs take C$0.40 billion. Attributable operating profit of C$5.28 billion at 7.5 times gives C$39.6 billion of enterprise value, about US$58.30 a share across 483 million shares. Add net cash of C$1.24 billion (US$1.83), the legacy royalty portfolio including the Fourmile net profits interest at a risk-weighted C$1.0 billion (US$1.47), and C$1.5 billion (US$2.21) for a discounted Quebrada Blanca-Collahuasi adjacency, and the standalone business is worth about US$63.70. Add Teck's 37.6% share of the US$800 million of announced annual corporate synergies capitalised at 8 times, roughly US$5 a share, and the figure is about US$69. Route two, the deal-terms anchor: 1.3301 Anglo American shares at 3,907 pence on 2026-08-04, converted at a sterling rate of 1.3443, is US$69.86 per Teck share. The two routes land within a dollar of each other, so US$70 is the base case.
risk_reward: From US$65.19 on 2026-08-04: the adverse case is US$32 a share (copper back to US$4.50 a pound, attributable operating profit halved to about C$3.1 billion, 6.5 times, net cash consumed by the Highland Valley build); the base case is US$70; the favourable case is US$81. There is no structural floor - the merger consideration is a fixed number of Anglo American shares, not a fixed sum of money, so it caps the relationship to Anglo American without protecting the absolute price, and net cash is only about US$1.83 a share. In plain terms the upside available to the base case is roughly the width of the merger spread, while the downside is a full copper cycle. That is the wrong shape at this price.
catalyst_status_note: Deal terms are fixed and the vote is done, so this is a spread, not an open-ended event. Anglo American and Teck announced a merger of equals on 2025-09-09 under which Teck shareholders receive 1.3301 Anglo American shares (or, for electing eligible Canadian holders, 1.3301 exchangeable shares) for each Class A or Class B share; Anglo American holders end with about 62.4% and Teck holders about 37.6%. Both shareholder bases approved on 2025-12-09. Investment Canada Act approval plus competition clearances from Canada, Chile, Australia, Japan, the European Union and the United States were confirmed on the fourth-quarter 2025 call (2026-02-19); South Korea cleared in the first quarter of 2026 (confirmed on the 2026-04-23 call). China is the single approval outstanding. Teck mailed the letter of transmittal and election form on 2026-06-30, named the future combined-company leadership team on 2026-07-30 - stating that completion is conditional on final regulatory approval and expected between September 2026 and March 2027 - and launched consent solicitations on six series of notes on 2026-08-03, which is the debt-side plumbing for a close. At Anglo American's 3,907 pence on 2026-08-04 and a sterling rate of 1.3443, the consideration is worth about US$69.86 per Teck share against US$65.19, a spread of roughly 7%. Per this lane's rules the status is descriptive and does not drive the verdict.
peer_comps_note: On corrected figures Teck's enterprise value is about C$43.1 billion (a US$31.5 billion equity value converted at 0.7105, less C$1.24 billion of net cash), which is about 6.7 times trailing operating profit before depreciation of C$6.47 billion and about 5.0 times the C$8.6 billion annualised from the first half of 2026. Against the assigned competitor set, verified on 2026-08-04: Freeport-McMoRan trades at 11.5 times trailing operating profit on a US$97.3 billion equity value, though its trailing denominator is depressed by the Grasberg disruption and flatters the multiple; Hudbay Minerals is at 6.6 times on a US$11.0 billion equity value; Southern Copper carries its perennial premium at a US$163.1 billion equity value; Ero Copper is US$3.0 billion, Ivanhoe Mines C$15.3 billion, Glencore GBP 64.4 billion and Anglo American GBP 41.9 billion. The 7.5 times used in the base case sits between Hudbay's clean print and Freeport's distorted one, which is the defensible middle for a producer with tier-one orebodies and net cash but a 40% minority in its best growth asset and a finite-life zinc tail at Red Dog. Note that all seven comparables rose 2-6% on 2026-08-04 alongside a copper price at its 52-week high, so every one of these multiples is being struck on a strong tape.
consensus_delta: The unusual feature here is that there is barely a consensus left to disagree with. Only one price target printed in the last quarter - Deutsche Bank at US$68 on 2026-07-02, when the shares were US$60.64 - against five in the past year averaging US$57. The stock at US$65.19 has already run past the average of the year's targets and to within 4% of the single fresh one. That thinness is not an accident: the sell side is migrating its copper models to Anglo American, because Teck as a separate listing has a finite life. So the honest statement of where we differ from the market is narrower and less flattering than the usual version of this section. We are not claiming the street has missed a hidden asset or mis-modelled a segment. We are claiming the street has stopped modelling at all, and that the price is now set by two things: the arithmetic of 1.3301 Anglo American shares, and the copper price. On the second of those we do disagree, and in the unpopular direction. At US$65.19 the shares discount a copper price of roughly US$5.90 a pound held indefinitely at a 7.5 times multiple, or the current US$6.65 spot at about 6.4 times. Neither is absurd, and both are above the US$5.75 we are willing to underwrite as mid-cycle. The market's error, if there is one, is optimism rather than neglect. Two genuine informational edges do exist and are worth naming precisely because they are small: the legacy royalty portfolio, including a 10% net profits interest rising to 15% over ground overlapping Barrick's Fourmile discovery, appears in no published valuation and management confirmed in April 2026 that it has no plan to monetise it; and the widely-circulated balance sheet data is simply wrong, showing net debt of C$3.74 billion where the company reports net cash of C$1.24 billion. Both are worth a few dollars a share. Neither changes the conclusion that the metal, not the mispricing, is what you are buying.
valley_of_death: The next three to nine months carry five identifiable stresses. First and largest: copper closed at US$6.65 a pound on 2026-08-04, its 52-week high and 53% above the US$4.36 low, and the entire copper complex rose 5-8% in that single session with Teck up 8.3%. A tape that moves that far that fast in one direction can move back. Teck's own torque measure says a 10% copper move swings operating profit by about 14%; a retracement merely to the middle of the 52-week range would take roughly a quarter of the earnings power out. Second: Chinese antitrust clearance is the only approval left and China is the dominant buyer of the concentrate this combination will control. A conditional approval with divestment or behavioural remedies is a known outcome for deals of this kind, and would widen the spread rather than close it. Third: free cash flow is being squeezed by design. Trailing free cash flow is C$1.52 billion against C$6.47 billion of operating profit before depreciation, a 24% conversion, because Highland Valley is in its peak capital year at C$900 million to C$1.2 billion, with a further C$450-500 million of capitalised stripping across the copper segment and diesel prices already flagged as a headwind. The net cash position is real but thin at C$1.24 billion, and it is being spent. Fourth: the Quebrada Blanca sand dam must reach steady state by year-end 2026. That objective has been restated on every call since the first quarter of 2025 and moved more than once; the secondary sand cyclone system was still only scheduled for 'the second half of this year' as of April 2026 and the permanent infrastructure timing remains 'under evaluation'. Fifth: the share buyback has been frozen since 2025-07-25 with roughly C$1.05 billion of the C$3.25 billion authorisation unused, so the company itself cannot support the shares into any of this. None of these is a solvency event. All of them can compress the price before the merger closes.
positioning_washout: The mechanical flow around this name is unusual and runs in both directions. On the sell side, Teck is a Canadian index constituent, and on closing its holders receive Anglo American plc shares - or, for electing eligible Canadian holders, exchangeable shares. If Standard and Poor's and the Toronto exchange do not resolve indexation for the combined company, Canadian index funds become forced, price-insensitive sellers at completion. Management has been chasing this since the announcement; in April 2026 the head of investor relations described 'green shoots' and an open consultation with, in her own words, no established timeline, and noted that these decisions are made quarterly. That is a dateable, large, mechanical seller that has not yet been defused. On the buy side, a combined company with a broader index footprint attracts global and UK index demand, and the merger arbitrage community has already arrived - the June 2026 institutional filings show Arrowstreet adding 48.4% to its position in the first quarter. There is, notably, no yield-driven washout left to come: the base dividend is C$0.125 a quarter, about a 0.5% yield, so income holders left long ago and cannot be shaken out again. The net judgement is that the forced-selling risk is concentrated at one identifiable moment - completion without a Canadian index solution - rather than spread through the period, and that the arbitrage base already in the stock will roll rather than liquidate.
forcing_function: Chinese antitrust clearance is the event. It is the single outstanding condition to a merger that both shareholder bases approved on 2025-12-09 and that has already cleared Canada, Chile, Australia, Japan, the European Union, the United States and South Korea. Anglo American and Teck said on 2026-07-30, when they named the future combined leadership team, that completion is conditional on receipt of final regulatory approval and expected between September 2026 and March 2027. The supporting mechanics are already moving: the letter of transmittal and election form went out on 2026-06-30, and consent solicitations on six series of Teck notes were launched on 2026-08-03. When clearance lands, the roughly 7% gap between Teck at US$65.19 and the US$69.86 that 1.3301 Anglo American shares are worth should close, and the security converts. A second, smaller forcing event sits alongside it - the Standard and Poor's and Toronto exchange decision on whether the combined company keeps Canadian index membership, taken on a quarterly cycle. Neither event re-rates the underlying business; both simply resolve a technical discount. The re-rating that would matter to a long-term holder - the combined company being valued as a top-five copper producer rather than as the sum of two mid-tier diversified miners - is a 2027 story that depends on the Quebrada Blanca-Collahuasi commercial agreement that does not yet exist.
moderator_conclusion: This is a good business at a full price, and the distinction is the whole decision. Take the operating case seriously first, because it deserves it. Teck spent 2025 failing publicly at Quebrada Blanca, then did something companies rarely do: it ran a formal operational review with outside technical experts and rebased its plans on demonstrated performance rather than design assumptions. Since then it has produced three consecutive stable quarters at that mine, reaffirmed multi-year guidance, cut copper net cash unit costs to US$1.64 a pound from US$2.02, more than doubled quarterly operating profit before depreciation to C$2.193 billion at a 61% margin, and beaten earnings estimates by a wide margin - all from a net cash balance sheet of C$1,244 million with C$10.3 billion of liquidity, while funding a two-decade life extension at Highland Valley. The reserve life is real and verified: Highland Valley to 2046 at an average 132,000 tonnes a year, Quebrada Blanca with a tax stability agreement to 2037 and a deposit management says supports multiple expansions, Red Dog still world-class though finite. The cost position is second-quartile and improving, which we have checked against company-reported figures rather than accepting the screener proxy - and on both cost and leverage the proxy is materially wrong, understating margin and, more seriously, showing net debt of C$3.74 billion where the company reports net cash of C$1.24 billion. Capital discipline, the sector's besetting sin, gets a mixed but improving grade: Quebrada Blanca's original capital blew out badly last cycle, Highland Valley's sanctioned figure came in 15-20% above the strategy-day estimate, but the steelmaking coal business was sold, C$1.3 billion was returned to shareholders in 2025, and the dividend is a modest C$0.50 a year rather than a top-of-cycle payout the company will later regret. Contracting is what it is for a concentrate producer: no long-term fixed-price offtake, sales into Asian and European smelters at benchmark treatment charges that are currently at historic lows and therefore in the miner's favour, with less than 20% of Red Dog concentrate exposed to China. Now the price. Copper printed US$6.65 a pound on 2026-08-04, the highest in a year and 53% off the low, and the whole cohort - Freeport, Southern Copper, Hudbay, Ero, Ivanhoe, Anglo, Glencore - rose together that session. Teck rose 8.3%. Our mid-cycle sum-of-the-parts at US$5.75 copper values the standalone business at about US$64 a share; adding Teck's share of the announced US$800 million of annual synergies takes it to roughly US$69, and the merger consideration of 1.3301 Anglo American shares is worth US$69.86 today. Two independent routes, both landing at about US$70, against a market price of US$65.19. That is 7% of upside, and it is the same 7% either way - the merger spread. Against it, the adverse case is US$32: copper back to US$4.50 a pound, which is where it traded a year ago, attributable operating profit falling from roughly C$5.3 billion to C$3.1 billion exactly as the 1.4-times torque predicts, a trough multiple of 6.5 times, and the net cash cushion consumed by the Highland Valley build. That is a 51% decline, and it lands within a dollar of Teck's own 52-week low. Nothing in the merger stops it, because the consideration is a fixed number of Anglo American shares, not a fixed sum of money, and Anglo American falls in the same tape. So the shape is roughly 7% up to fair value against 51% down to a cycle that has happened twice in five years. We are not paid for that. The verdict is to wait rather than to buy, and the level is specific: US$52 a share, which is a 20% discount to our base case, restores our standalone valuation with a real margin of safety, and would require copper somewhere near US$5.25-5.50 a pound. Below that we would want the position and would size it as a core holding rather than a trade. On the value case judged alone - price against our sum-of-the-parts, plus the quality of the numbers, ignoring the deal entirely - the shares offer no discount at all today, which is why that score is lower than the overall one: the business has improved, the price has improved faster. One last thing worth carrying forward, because it is the sort of item that becomes interesting at a lower price: the legacy royalty portfolio, and specifically the 10% net profits interest rising to 15% over ground overlapping Barrick's Fourmile gold discovery in Nevada, is in nobody's model, was described by the chief executive in April 2026 as valuable with no plan to sell it, and by press estimate could generate US$100-200 million a year at full production. It is worth a few dollars a share and it comes free.
